correctness.rationale: The exact nearest-vertex cell is the angular sector of a regular polygon centered on each radius; it splits into 2n congruent right triangles with vertex V as nearest site. Vertex-polar radial integration gives the stated integral with sin(a)^(p+1)/cos(a), and differentiating cos(t)/sin(t)^(p+1) proves the integration-by-parts moment identity. Beta-integral convergence for p<1, J_1(a)=log cot(a/2), and a local power singularity for p>1 yield the sharp constants. For p=1+λ/L, uniform bounded-λ control of sin(t)^(−p)−t^(−p) gives J_p=L(e^λ−1)/λ+O_B(1); multiplying by a^(p+1) cancels e^λ to give (1−e^(−λ))/(3λ), uniformly on compact λ. Twenty independently integrated formula comparisons, second-moment reduction, and five finite crossover cases corroborated the exact computation; the slower O(1/L) finite crossover convergence is not a theorem failure. Every n≥3, p>0 is included, no irregular geometry is claimed.
